title: Tiered Thrift Bands: Budget Gating + Micro-Quant Rollout Charter
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Introduce a tiered budgeting and rollout mechanism ("Thrift Bands") that gates cost-saving mechanisms (micro-quant profiles, TTL-prefetch) by dynamic budget slices per customer group. The charter covers configuration surface in Console, server-side gating logic, runtime profiles, and monitoring/alerting required for safe automated rollouts.

Scope:
- Define 3 thrift bands (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive) with explicit token-econ budgets and feature gating rules.
- Support micro-quant profiles (q4/q8-like) per model variant with per-band fallbacks.
- TTL-based prefetch gating with adaptive TTLs per band and per-route heuristics.
- Console UI to define bands, budgets, and rollout policies; API for programmatic control.
- Canary rollout orchestration (0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated rollback triggers.

Success metrics (KPIs):
- 20% reduction in per-token cost for Balanced band workloads in 90 days vs baseline.
- <2% increase in customer-facing latency P95 for Conservative/Balanced bands.
- No customer-facing quality regressions above threshold (qa_regressions > 0.5% triggers rollback).

Milestones:
- 2026-02-12: Draft PRD & experiment matrix (done)
- 2026-02-22: Core runtime gating prototype merged (ENG-84521)
- 2026-03-05: Console controls UI mock approved by Design (DES-1482)
- 2026-03-10: Canary automation orchestration integrated with rollout service (In Progress)
- 2026-03-24: Field trial with internal beta customers (target)
- 2026-04-10: Beta evaluation & final sweep for release

Rollout plan and safety gates:
- Start with internal tenant + 2 low-risk customers (0.5%). Monitor token-econ, latency, and quality signals for 48h.
- Move to 5% if no red flags; run 7-day extended eval at 25% before full rollout.
- Safety triggers: (1) latency P95 > baseline + 20%, (2) quality regression > 0.5% on monitored prompt set, (3) error rate spike > 0.3%. Any trigger auto-rolls back and creates ENG incident.

Monitoring & dashboards:
- New dashboard: "Thrift Bands — Live" (Console) showing per-band cost delta, latency distributions, quality regressions (by prompt set), and per-customer adoption.
- Alerts: Pager for SRE on safety triggers; channel #econ-ops for PM/Eng notifications.

Dependencies:
- ENG-84012: Rollout service canary hooks (blocking for automation)
- ENG-85877: Micro-quant kernel selection & compatibility mapping
- DES-1482: Console control mockups and accessibility review
- PM-77123: Customer opt-in consent flow and billing notes

Open decisions & tradeoffs:
- Band count and names: kept to 3 to reduce complexity; can add custom bands later.
- Aggressive band will use micro-quant by default; risk of quality regression mitigated by per-route QA sets and hot rollback.
- TTL-prefetch adaptive logic initially heuristic-based; long-term plan to use model-driven prediction if heuristics underperform.

Acceptance criteria for MVP:
- Console: Create/Edit thrift bands + assign rollout policy (boolean + percentage controls)
- Runtime: Band-aware kernel selection and TTL-prefetch gating live behind feature flag
- Orchestration: Canary automation able to progress/rollback on defined triggers
- Observability: Live dashboard and alerts configured; baseline collection for 7 days

Notes on uniqueness: This charter focuses on the orchestration layer that ties discrete cost controls (quant profiles, TTL-prefetch) into a single per-customer budget gating abstraction ("bands") to make economic controls predictable, reversible, and observable. Unlike previous one-off tactics, the Thrift Bands aim to standardize how we expose cost-EDL tradeoffs to customers and for internal automation.
